**Chapter 3:** PROBABILITY & STATISTICS FOR MACHINE LEARNING - PART 1

Author: Your ML Tutor
Date: December 4, 2025
Module: Mathematical Foundations - Probability & Statistics

Topics Covered (Part 1):
1. Basic Probability Concepts
2. Random Variables
3. Probability Distributions (Discrete)
4. Probability Distributions (Continuous)

Why Probability & Statistics in ML?

- Uncertainty: Real-world data is noisy and uncertain
- Inference: Make predictions with confidence levels
- Learning: Probabilistic models (Naive Bayes, Bayesian Networks)
- Evaluation: Statistical significance, hypothesis testing
- Generalization: Understanding model performance

sections.title: simulate_coin_flips()
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Simulate coin flips and track probability of heads
- SECTION 2: RANDOM VARIABLES…
- SECTION 3: DISCRETE PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS…
- SECTION 4: CONTINUOUS PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS…
- Example 1: Simulate coin flips to show law of large numbers
- Visualize Law of Large Numbers
- Plot 1: Convergence to true probability
- Plot 2: Sample space visualization

Simulate coin flips and track probability of heads

```python
# Example 1: Simulate coin flips to show law of large numbers
def simulate_coin_flips(n_flips):
    """Simulate coin flips and track probability of heads"""
    flips = np.random.randint(0, 2, n_flips)  # 0=Tails, 1=Heads
    cumulative_heads = np.cumsum(flips)
    trials = np.arange(1, n_flips + 1)
    probability = cumulative_heads / trials
    return trials, probability

# Simulate
np.random.seed(42)
trials, prob = simulate_coin_flips(10000)

# Visualize Law of Large Numbers
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Convergence to true probability
axes[0, 0].plot(trials, prob, alpha=0.7, linewidth=1)
axes[0, 0].axhline(y=0.5, color='r', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label='True P(Heads) = 0.5')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Number of Flips', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Observed P(Heads)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title('Law of Large Numbers: Coin Flips', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Sample space visualization
outcomes = ['Heads', 'Tails']
probabilities = [0.5, 0.5]
colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4']
axes[0, 1].bar(outcomes, probabilities, color=colors, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Fair Coin: Sample Space', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_ylim(0, 1)
for i, (outcome, prob_val) in enumerate(zip(outcomes, probabilities)):
    axes[0, 1].text(i, prob_val + 0.05, f'P = {prob_val}', ha='center', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 3: Venn diagram for probability rules
from matplotlib.patches import Circle
axes[1, 0].set_xlim(0, 10)
axes[1, 0].set_ylim(0, 10)
axes[1, 0].set_aspect('equal')

# Draw circles for A and B
circle_A = Circle((3.5, 5), 2, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Event A')
circle_B = Circle((6.5, 5), 2, color='blue', alpha=0.3, label='Event B')
axes[1, 0].add_patch(circle_A)
axes[1, 0].add_patch(circle_B)

# Labels
axes[1, 0].text(2.5, 5, 'A', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].text(7.5, 5, 'B', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].text(5, 5, 'A∩B', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].text(5, 1, 'P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)', fontsize=12, 
                ha='center', bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='yellow', alpha=0.5))

axes[1, 0].set_title('Addition Rule: Union of Events', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].axis('off')

# Plot 4: Independence visualization
sample_size = 1000
coin1 = np.random.randint(0, 2, sample_size)
coin2 = np.random.randint(0, 2, sample_size)

# Create contingency table
hh = np.sum((coin1 == 1) & (coin2 == 1))
ht = np.sum((coin1 == 1) & (coin2 == 0))
th = np.sum((coin1 == 0) & (coin2 == 1))
tt = np.sum((coin1 == 0) & (coin2 == 0))

contingency = np.array([[hh, ht], [th, tt]])
axes[1, 1].imshow(contingency, cmap='YlOrRd', alpha=0.7)
axes[1, 1].set_xticks([0, 1])
axes[1, 1].set_yticks([0, 1])
axes[1, 1].set_xticklabels(['Coin2: H', 'Coin2: T'])
axes[1, 1].set_yticklabels(['Coin1: H', 'Coin1: T'])
axes[1, 1].set_title('Independence: Two Coins', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

# Add counts
for i in range(2):
    for j in range(2):
        axes[1, 1].text(j, i, f'{contingency[i, j]}', ha='center', va='center', 
                       fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', color='white')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('probability_basics.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved probability basics visualization")

# Show key probabilities
print(f"\nAfter {trials[-1]} flips:")
print(f"  Observed P(Heads) = {prob[-1]:.4f}")
print(f"  True P(Heads) = 0.5000")
print(f"  Difference = {abs(prob[-1] - 0.5):.4f}")

print(f"\nIndependence check (two coins):")
print(f"  P(H,H) observed = {hh/sample_size:.3f}")
print(f"  P(H)·P(H) expected = {0.5*0.5:.3f}")
print(f"  Match? {abs(hh/sample_size - 0.25) < 0.05}")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 2: RANDOM VARIABLES
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
Random Variable = Function that maps outcomes to numbers

Roll a die:    1  2  3  4  5  6  ← Outcomes
               ↓  ↓  ↓  ↓  ↓  ↓
X (value):     1  2  3  4  5  6  ← Random Variable
P(X):        1/6 1/6 1/6 1/6 1/6 1/6 ← Probability

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Random Variable (RV) assigns a number to each random outcome:
• Discrete RV: Countable values (die roll, coin flips)
• Continuous RV: Uncountable values (height, temperature)

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• X = number of emails per hour
• Y = time until next customer arrives
• Z = height of randomly selected person
• W = stock price tomorrow

KEY CONCEPTS:
-------------
1. Probability Mass Function (PMF) - Discrete
   P(X = x) = probability X takes value x
   
2. Probability Density Function (PDF) - Continuous
   P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫[a,b] f(x)dx
   
3. Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)
   F(x) = P(X ≤ x)
   
4. Expected Value (Mean)
   E[X] = Σ x·P(X=x)  (discrete)
   E[X] = ∫ x·f(x)dx  (continuous)
   
5. Variance
   Var(X) = E[(X - μ)²] = E[X²] - (E[X])²
   
6. Standard Deviation
   σ = √Var(X)

MATH:
-----
Properties:
• E[aX + b] = aE[X] + b
• Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X)
• E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y]
• Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) (if independent)
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 2: RANDOM VARIABLES")
print("="*80)

# Example: Die roll random variable
die_outcomes = np.arange(1, 7)
die_probs = np.ones(6) / 6

# Calculations
expected_value = np.sum(die_outcomes * die_probs)
expected_x_squared = np.sum(die_outcomes**2 * die_probs)
variance = expected_x_squared - expected_value**2
std_dev = np.sqrt(variance)

# Cumulative probabilities
cdf = np.cumsum(die_probs)

# Visualize
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: PMF (Probability Mass Function)
axes[0, 0].bar(die_outcomes, die_probs, color='steelblue', alpha=0.7, 
               edgecolor='black', linewidth=2, width=0.8)
axes[0, 0].axvline(expected_value, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = {expected_value:.2f}')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Outcome (x)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('P(X = x)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title('PMF: Fair Die Roll', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].set_xticks(die_outcomes)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 2: CDF (Cumulative Distribution Function)
axes[0, 1].step(die_outcomes, cdf, where='post', color='darkgreen', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].scatter(die_outcomes, cdf, color='darkgreen', s=100, zorder=3)
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Outcome (x)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('P(X ≤ x)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('CDF: Fair Die Roll', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xticks(die_outcomes)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 1].set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)

# Plot 3: Simulation showing convergence to expected value
n_rolls = 10000
rolls = np.random.randint(1, 7, n_rolls)
cumulative_mean = np.cumsum(rolls) / np.arange(1, n_rolls + 1)

axes[1, 0].plot(cumulative_mean, alpha=0.7, linewidth=1.5)
axes[1, 0].axhline(expected_value, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = {expected_value:.2f}')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Number of Rolls', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Sample Mean', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Law of Large Numbers: Die Rolls', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Variance visualization
axes[1, 1].bar(die_outcomes, die_probs, color='lightblue', alpha=0.7, 
               edgecolor='black', linewidth=2, width=0.8)
axes[1, 1].axvline(expected_value, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'μ = {expected_value:.2f}')
axes[1, 1].axvspan(expected_value - std_dev, expected_value + std_dev, 
                   alpha=0.2, color='red', label=f'σ = {std_dev:.2f}')

# Show deviations
for x in die_outcomes:
    deviation = x - expected_value
    axes[1, 1].plot([x, x], [0, die_probs[x-1]], 'k-', alpha=0.3, linewidth=1)
    if abs(deviation) > 0.1:
        axes[1, 1].annotate('', xy=(expected_value, die_probs[x-1]/2), 
                           xytext=(x, die_probs[x-1]/2),
                           arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='orange', lw=2))

axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Outcome (x)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('P(X = x)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Mean & Standard Deviation', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 1].set_xticks(die_outcomes)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('random_variables.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved random variables visualization")

print(f"\nDie Roll Random Variable:")
print(f"  E[X] (Expected Value) = {expected_value:.4f}")
print(f"  Var(X) (Variance) = {variance:.4f}")
print(f"  σ (Std Deviation) = {std_dev:.4f}")
print(f"\nAfter {n_rolls} rolls:")
print(f"  Sample mean = {cumulative_mean[-1]:.4f}")
print(f"  Converged? {abs(cumulative_mean[-1] - expected_value) < 0.01}")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 3: DISCRETE PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
Common patterns in random phenomena:

Bernoulli: Single trial    🎯 → Hit or Miss
Binomial: Multiple trials  🎯🎯🎯 → Count successes
Poisson: Rare events       ⭐ → Events per time period

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Discrete distributions model countable outcomes:
• Bernoulli: One trial (coin flip)
• Binomial: n trials (n coin flips)
• Poisson: Events in interval (emails per hour)
• Geometric: Trials until success

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Bernoulli: User clicks ad (yes/no)
• Binomial: 10 users, how many click?
• Poisson: Number of server requests per second
• Geometric: Rolls until first six

KEY DISTRIBUTIONS:
------------------

1. BERNOULLI (Single trial)
   X ~ Bernoulli(p)
   P(X=1) = p, P(X=0) = 1-p
   E[X] = p, Var(X) = p(1-p)
   
2. BINOMIAL (n trials)
   X ~ Binomial(n, p)
   P(X=k) = C(n,k) · p^k · (1-p)^(n-k)
   E[X] = np, Var(X) = np(1-p)
   
3. POISSON (Rate λ)
   X ~ Poisson(λ)
   P(X=k) = (λ^k · e^(-λ)) / k!
   E[X] = λ, Var(X) = λ
   
4. GEOMETRIC (Trials to success)
   X ~ Geometric(p)
   P(X=k) = (1-p)^(k-1) · p
   E[X] = 1/p, Var(X) = (1-p)/p²

MATH:
-----
Binomial coefficient: C(n,k) = n! / (k!(n-k)!)
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 3: DISCRETE PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS")
print("="*80)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Distribution 1: Bernoulli
p_bernoulli = 0.7
x_bern = [0, 1]
pmf_bern = [1-p_bernoulli, p_bernoulli]

axes[0, 0].bar(x_bern, pmf_bern, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4'], alpha=0.7, 
               edgecolor='black', linewidth=2, width=0.4)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Outcome', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title(f'Bernoulli Distribution (p={p_bernoulli})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xticks([0, 1])
axes[0, 0].set_xticklabels(['Failure (0)', 'Success (1)'])
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')
for i, (x, prob) in enumerate(zip(x_bern, pmf_bern)):
    axes[0, 0].text(x, prob + 0.03, f'{prob:.2f}', ha='center', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# Distribution 2: Binomial
n_trials = 10
p_binomial = 0.5
x_binom = np.arange(0, n_trials + 1)
pmf_binom = [comb(n_trials, k) * (p_binomial**k) * ((1-p_binomial)**(n_trials-k)) 
             for k in x_binom]

axes[0, 1].bar(x_binom, pmf_binom, color='steelblue', alpha=0.7, 
               edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
axes[0, 1].axvline(n_trials * p_binomial, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = {n_trials * p_binomial:.1f}')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Number of Successes (k)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title(f'Binomial Distribution (n={n_trials}, p={p_binomial})', 
                     fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Distribution 3: Poisson
lambda_poisson = 3.5
x_poisson = np.arange(0, 15)
pmf_poisson = [(lambda_poisson**k * np.exp(-lambda_poisson)) / math.factorial(k) 
               for k in x_poisson]

axes[1, 0].bar(x_poisson, pmf_poisson, color='darkgreen', alpha=0.7, 
               edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
axes[1, 0].axvline(lambda_poisson, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = λ = {lambda_poisson}')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Number of Events (k)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title(f'Poisson Distribution (λ={lambda_poisson})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Distribution 4: Geometric
p_geometric = 0.3
x_geom = np.arange(1, 16)
pmf_geom = [(1-p_geometric)**(k-1) * p_geometric for k in x_geom]

axes[1, 1].bar(x_geom, pmf_geom, color='purple', alpha=0.7, 
               edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
axes[1, 1].axvline(1/p_geometric, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = {1/p_geometric:.2f}')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Trial Number (k)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title(f'Geometric Distribution (p={p_geometric})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('discrete_distributions.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved discrete distributions visualization")

# Print statistics
print(f"\nDistribution Statistics:")
print(f"\n1. Bernoulli(p={p_bernoulli}):")
print(f"   E[X] = {p_bernoulli:.2f}")
print(f"   Var(X) = {p_bernoulli * (1-p_bernoulli):.4f}")

print(f"\n2. Binomial(n={n_trials}, p={p_binomial}):")
print(f"   E[X] = {n_trials * p_binomial:.2f}")
print(f"   Var(X) = {n_trials * p_binomial * (1-p_binomial):.4f}")
print(f"   P(X = 5) = {pmf_binom[5]:.4f}")

print(f"\n3. Poisson(λ={lambda_poisson}):")
print(f"   E[X] = {lambda_poisson:.2f}")
print(f"   Var(X) = {lambda_poisson:.2f}")
print(f"   P(X = 3) = {pmf_poisson[3]:.4f}")

print(f"\n4. Geometric(p={p_geometric}):")
print(f"   E[X] = {1/p_geometric:.2f}")
print(f"   Var(X) = {(1-p_geometric)/p_geometric**2:.4f}")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 4: CONTINUOUS PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
Continuous distributions have smooth curves:

         PDF
          ▲
       ┌──┴──┐
      ╱       ╲     ← Bell curve (Normal)
     ╱         ╲
────┴───────────┴──→ x

Area under curve = Probability!

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Continuous RV can take any value in an interval:
• Normal (Gaussian): Most common, bell-shaped
• Uniform: All values equally likely
• Exponential: Waiting times, decay
• Beta: Probabilities themselves

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Normal: Heights, test scores, errors
• Uniform: Random number generators
• Exponential: Time between events
• Beta: Click-through rates, conversion rates

KEY DISTRIBUTIONS:
------------------

1. UNIFORM (Flat)
   X ~ Uniform(a, b)
   f(x) = 1/(b-a) for a ≤ x ≤ b
   E[X] = (a+b)/2, Var(X) = (b-a)²/12
   
2. NORMAL (Gaussian)
   X ~ N(μ, σ²)
   f(x) = (1/√(2πσ²)) · exp(-(x-μ)²/(2σ²))
   E[X] = μ, Var(X) = σ²
   
3. EXPONENTIAL
   X ~ Exp(λ)
   f(x) = λe^(-λx) for x ≥ 0
   E[X] = 1/λ, Var(X) = 1/λ²
   
4. BETA
   X ~ Beta(α, β)
   Complex formula, defined on [0,1]
   E[X] = α/(α+β)

SPECIAL: Standard Normal Z ~ N(0,1)
• 68% within 1σ
• 95% within 2σ  
• 99.7% within 3σ (68-95-99.7 rule)

MATH:
-----
For continuous RV:
• P(X = x) = 0 (single point has no area!)
• P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫[a,b] f(x)dx
• CDF: F(x) = P(X ≤ x) = ∫[-∞,x] f(t)dt
• PDF: f(x) = dF(x)/dx
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 4: CONTINUOUS PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS")
print("="*80)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Distribution 1: Uniform
a, b = 2, 8
x_uniform = np.linspace(0, 10, 1000)
pdf_uniform = np.where((x_uniform >= a) & (x_uniform <= b), 1/(b-a), 0)

axes[0, 0].plot(x_uniform, pdf_uniform, 'b-', linewidth=2.5)
axes[0, 0].fill_between(x_uniform, 0, pdf_uniform, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 0].axvline((a+b)/2, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = {(a+b)/2}')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('x', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('f(x)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title(f'Uniform Distribution U({a}, {b})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 0].set_ylim(0, 0.25)

# Distribution 2: Normal (Gaussian)
mu, sigma = 0, 1
x_normal = np.linspace(-4, 4, 1000)
pdf_normal = (1/(sigma * np.sqrt(2*np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5*((x_normal - mu)/sigma)**2)

axes[0, 1].plot(x_normal, pdf_normal, 'g-', linewidth=2.5, label='PDF')
axes[0, 1].fill_between(x_normal, 0, pdf_normal, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 1].axvline(mu, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label=f'μ = {mu}')

# Show standard deviations
for i in [1, 2, 3]:
    axes[0, 1].axvline(mu + i*sigma, color='orange', linestyle=':', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7)
    axes[0, 1].axvline(mu - i*sigma, color='orange', linestyle=':', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7)

# Shade 68-95-99.7 regions
x_1sigma = x_normal[(x_normal >= mu-sigma) & (x_normal <= mu+sigma)]
pdf_1sigma = (1/(sigma * np.sqrt(2*np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5*((x_1sigma - mu)/sigma)**2)
axes[0, 1].fill_between(x_1sigma, 0, pdf_1sigma, alpha=0.5, color='yellow', label='68% (±1σ)')

axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('x', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('f(x)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title(f'Normal Distribution N({mu}, {sigma}²)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Distribution 3: Exponential
lambda_exp = 1.5
x_exp = np.linspace(0, 5, 1000)
pdf_exp = lambda_exp * np.exp(-lambda_exp * x_exp)

axes[1, 0].plot(x_exp, pdf_exp, 'r-', linewidth=2.5)
axes[1, 0].fill_between(x_exp, 0, pdf_exp, alpha=0.3, color='red')
axes[1, 0].axvline(1/lambda_exp, color='blue', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'E[X] = {1/lambda_exp:.2f}')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('x', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('f(x)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title(f'Exponential Distribution (λ={lambda_exp})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Distribution 4: Beta (multiple shapes)
x_beta = np.linspace(0, 1, 1000)
beta_params = [(0.5, 0.5), (2, 2), (2, 5), (5, 2)]
colors = ['purple', 'green', 'blue', 'red']

for (alpha, beta_param), color in zip(beta_params, colors):
    pdf_beta = stats.beta.pdf(x_beta, alpha, beta_param)
    axes[1, 1].plot(x_beta, pdf_beta, linewidth=2, label=f'α={alpha}, β={beta_param}', color=color)
    axes[1, 1].fill_between(x_beta, 0, pdf_beta, alpha=0.2, color=color)

axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('x', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('f(x)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Beta Distribution (Various Parameters)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('continuous_distributions.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

print(f"   Var(X) = {1/lambda_exp**2:.4f}")
```
